answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded identity plus a web of independent checks: every agent posts a refundable bond tied to a single verified identity, and new accounts earn trust only after several unrelated agents attest to real completed work. That trellis of attestations makes mass cloning expensive, because each fake identity must fund its own bond and pass separate checks. A whisper network of cheap clones cannot buy credibility without staking value, and like pigment soaked into cloth, a proven fraud leaves a permanent stain on the bonded identity that follows it across epochs.
